claims.text: P10: for every synthetic archetype x risk profile, plain and with every feature (director, own accounts, cash, lenders, acquirers), the pseudonymised statement and profile give identical per-line categories/rules/reversals, figures M1-M28 (buckets included), monthly cells and indicators under both v1 and v2; plus hand-built cases (director inside an own-account name, two spellings, ambiguous both-kinds credit, round trips, returned DD, gambling, a profile name holding lender wording).

R46 CLI: `cma pseudonymise FILE --format F --out DIR [--profile CASE]` converts through the format's importer (csv, monzo, openbanking, truelayer, bank-csv:PROFILE), writes statement.csv, case.yaml (tokenised profile), PSEUDONYMISED.txt and pseudonymised.json into a new owner-only folder, labels every output as pseudonymised personal data, not anonymous data, never writes the token mapping, keeps every id/date/amount/balance, refuses to overwrite, and writes nothing for a refused statement.
Full suite passes with the change.

claims.proof_cmd: ruff check src tests && python -m compileall -q src

notes: Committed as 766e408 on bridgie-task/statement-review/T39. How the copy keeps P10: every span the v1 or v2 rules match (their patterns, and their unless/requires exceptions), the gambling operators, invoice references and the bank wording the counterparty normaliser strips (RAIL_PREFIX, OUTGOING_TRANSFER, trailing DD) are kept as they are. Case-profile names (directors, shareholders, own accounts, business name) are found with the categoriser's own name pattern. Each region they cover is replaced by the tokens of exactly the names found there, so a director inside an own-account name still matches both. A second spelling of one region gets a variant token, so counterparties group as they did before. Every other word becomes one token per distinct word: 8 letters for a word of letters, digits for a word with a digit, so counterparty() strips digit words as before. A profile name that overlaps recognised wording (a director called IWOCA) is kept unpseudonymised, and the manifest counts such names. Before anything is written, the copy is categorised and computed under v1 and v2 and compared with the original line by line, figure by figure, month by month and indicator by indicator. Any difference refuses it, naming only the figure or line id, and nothing is written. Scope limits: P10 is checked without firm rules or overrides, since a firm rule's regex may name a counterparty that the copy tokenises. P10 is checked one statement at a time, since `cma pseudonymise` takes one file. Descriptions in the copy are in the categoriser's folded form (NFC, upper case). The profile label becomes 'PSEUDONYMISED <token>'. Two profile names that differ only by separators share a token, as the categoriser already treats them as one name.
